_sobre: Quem fala cada trecho das frases com fala de personagem (texto no formato do campo `fala` de docs/narracao/frases-dom-quixote-parte-2-en.json, sem mudar palavras). Frases fora daqui são da NARRADORA. Elenco em ../elenco.json.
p1-s2: Don’t run away, you cowardly giants!
p1-s3: Only one knight is coming to fight you all!
he shouted, charging at the first windmill in the field!
p1-s6: Sancho came rushing up on his donkey, holding his head in a fright:
p1-s7: Didn’t I tell you they were only windmills?
p1-s8: But Don Quixote shook off the dust, straightened his dented basin and explained, very calmly:
p1-s9: In a knight’s adventures, everything changes in the blink of an eye!
p1-s10: It was the wicked wizard Frestón who cast a spell and turned the giants into windmills, just to steal my victory.
p1-s11: But no magic can beat our courage!
p2-s2: A true knight never gives in to sadness!
he said, patting his loyal Rocinante.
p2-s4: A hero of Spain long ago lost his sword in a battle, so he fought with a tree trunk and won!
p2-s5: And I shall do just the same!
p3-s5: Here, what belongs to one belongs to all!
p3-s8: Holding the acorns in his hand, Don Quixote spoke with great feeling:
Once there was a very happy time, the golden age, when nobody built fences and everybody knew how to share the fruits of the earth with love!
p4-s3: cried the knight, full of joy.
p4-s5: On the left comes the terrible Alifanfarón of Trapobana; on the right, brave Pentapolín of the Rolled-Up Sleeve, who always fights with his sleeves rolled up!
p4-s6: said Sancho, listening hard and frowning,
I can’t hear any swords or trumpets, just lots of baaaa!
p5-s4: said Sancho kindly, with a cheeky smile,
you have the saddest, sorriest face I have ever seen in my life!
p5-s5: I think your hero’s name should be the Knight of the sorrowful face!
p5-s8: All the great knights in books have names like poems.
p5-s9: I shall have a noble, thoughtful face painted on my shield!
p6-s5: Don Quixote grabbed his lance at once:
p6-s6: Come out, giant of the dark!
p6-s9: Once upon a time there was a shepherd called Lope Ruiz, who had to take three hundred goats to the other side of a very deep river.
p6-s10: But he only had a teeny-tiny boat, with room for just one goat at a time!
p6-s11: Now, listen carefully and don’t forget to count every little goat that crosses... because if you lose count, the story stops right there!
p7-s8: When he saw that he had been scared for nothing, Sancho couldn’t help it: he held his tummy and let out such a big laugh that it echoed across the hills, and he nearly fell off his donkey:
p7-s9: The giant of the night was a hammer for beating cloth!
p8-s4: Don Quixote’s eyes went wide with wonder:
Look, Sancho, the greatest treasure in the world!
p8-s5: That warrior is wearing the famous helmet of mambrino, the magic helmet that makes whoever wears it unbeatable!
p8-s8: cried the poor barber, terrified of that man in armour.
